# MDL312 · `control-character`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

A line contains an invisible control character.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | values |
| Default severity | warning |
| Fix | — |
| Design references | K2, K17, cases 31, 57, 60, 66 |

## Why

Control characters are invisible in editors and reviews, and GLib gives some of them surprising meanings:

- a NUL byte at the start of a line turns the whole line into a comment: the key silently disappears;
- a NUL byte in a value cuts the value there;
- a vertical tab (`\v`) is not whitespace for GLib: `\vroutines=1` defines the key `\vroutines`, not `routines`.

NUL bytes that make a line unparsable are reported by MDL111; carriage returns by MDL103.

## Example

❌ Before:

```text
[mydumper]
# \x1bred
threads=4
```

(`\r`, `\t` and `\xHH` stand for the bytes they name, `·` for a trailing space)

```text
2:3-2:4 warning MDL312[control-character] control character U+001B ESCAPE in this line
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL312: warning   # or error, info, off
```

To accept one occurrence, put `# mydumper-lint: disable-next-line=MDL312` on the line above it.
